title: Statistical power = 1 - beta (probability of detecting a true difference)
vignette: Investigators design a randomized controlled trial comparing a new drug (drug B) with standard therapy for reducing mortality in patients with ST-elevation myocardial infarction. Before enrolling patients, the researchers want to ensure that, if a true difference in mortality actually exists between the two treatments, the study has a high probability of detecting that difference. Which of the following statistical concepts best represents this probability?

clues.text: if a true difference in mortality actually exists
clues.note: The premise is that the alternative hypothesis is TRUE (a real difference exists) - the setting in which power and type II error are defined.

clues.text: high probability of detecting that difference
clues.note: The probability of correctly detecting a true difference (rejecting a false null hypothesis) is the definition of statistical power = 1 - beta.

whatMatters: The probability of correctly detecting a true difference when one exists is statistical POWER = 1 - beta. Answer E. Beta is the probability of MISSING a true difference (type II error); power is its complement.
strategy: Anchor on the definition: power (1 - beta) = probability of rejecting the null when the alternative is true = detecting a real effect. Distinguish from beta / type II error (failing to detect a true effect) and from alpha / type I error / p-value (false-positive concepts about rejecting a TRUE null).

eliminations.label: Alpha - the false-positive threshold
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: alpha is the pre-set significance level (commonly 0.05), the acceptable probability of a type I error. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it concerns wrongly rejecting a TRUE null (false positive), not detecting a true difference. ✅ Correct if: asking about the significance threshold / false-positive rate.

eliminations.label: Beta - probability of MISSING a true difference
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: beta is the probability of a type II error - failing to detect a difference that truly exists. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is the complement of power; the question asks for detecting the difference, which is 1 - beta. ✅ Correct if: asking about the chance of a false-negative result.

eliminations.label: p-value - probability under the null, not power
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the probability of observing data as/more extreme than seen IF the null were true. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a result computed from one study, not the pre-study probability of detecting a real effect. ✅ Correct if: interpreting statistical significance of an observed result.

eliminations.label: Type II error - the error, not the detection probability (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a type II (beta) error is concluding there is NO difference when one truly exists (false negative). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: detecting the true difference is the OPPOSITE - power (1 - beta). ✅ Correct if: naming the error of missing a real effect.

eliminations.label: Type I error - false positive
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a type I (alpha) error is concluding there IS a difference when none truly exists. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is a false-positive error, unrelated to correctly detecting a real difference. ✅ Correct if: naming the error of a false-positive finding.

reasoning: Premise: a true difference actually exists (alternative hypothesis true)
Probability of correctly detecting it = rejecting a false null = statistical power
Power = 1 - beta (beta = probability of missing the true difference)
mechanism: Hypothesis testing has two error types. A type I error (alpha) is a false positive - rejecting a true null hypothesis (concluding a difference exists when it does not); alpha is the pre-set significance level. A type II error (beta) is a false negative - failing to reject a false null (missing a difference that truly exists). Statistical POWER is the probability of correctly rejecting a false null - i.e., detecting a true effect when it is present - and equals 1 - beta. Power increases with larger sample size, larger true effect size, lower variability, and a higher (less stringent) alpha. This trial's stated goal ('high probability of detecting a true difference if one exists') is precisely power = 1 - beta. The p-value is a separate concept: the probability of the observed (or more extreme) data assuming the null is true, used to judge significance of a completed study.

difficulty.label: 📚 Pure knowledge gap
difficulty.message: First Aid Biostat > power = 1 - beta = P(detect true effect); type I error = alpha (false positive), type II error = beta (false negative); power increases with n, effect size, and alpha.

difficulty.label: 🧭 Understanding the question
difficulty.message: 'Detect a true difference if it exists' is the verbal definition of power (1 - beta).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocabulary
difficulty.message: Unsure on power, beta, alpha, type I vs type II error, or p-value? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🧲 Pulled by a distractor
difficulty.message: Beta and type II error are the OPPOSITE (missing the effect); alpha/type I/p-value are false-positive/null-based concepts.

difficulty.label: ✍️ Something else
difficulty.message: Bank: power = 1 - beta; increase power with bigger sample, bigger effect size, less variability, higher alpha.

memoryHook: Power is the study's eyesight: 1 - beta = the chance it SEES a real difference. Beta is the blind spot that misses it.
